sentences.text: The petitioner has filed claim application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02. The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
On 28.11.2021 when the petitioner was going towards his Village Channarayapura from Devarayasamudra by riding a Honda Dio bearing No.KA-07-Y-6601, on correct side of the road.

On the way, at about 08.30 a.m, when he was going near Nallur Gate on Mulabagal - Kolar NH-75 Road, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, one Goods Tempo bearing No.TN-91-AZ-6539 was going ahead of the petitioner's scooter,
driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden applied brake (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 unmindfully and stopped the goods tempo in the middle of the road, without exhibiting any indications or signal.
The petitioner inspite of taking due care and caution, he could not able to avoid dashing his scooter against the stopped goods tempo from behind.

Due to this the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately taken to R.L. Jalappa hospital,
Kolar, wherein after two days of treatment, he was shifted to Jyotsna hospital, T.C.
Palya Road, Bengaluru, in turn to Chaya Super Speciality hospital, B.Channasandra Main Road, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and discharged on 24.12.2021.
On 31.12.2021 he was admitted to SNR hospital, Kolar, for further management.

He was treated conservatively as an inpatient and discharged on 13.02.2022 and till today he is under treatment as an outpatient and has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc., and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 38 years and was an agriculturist and dhobi and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he is bedridden and lost his income.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending goods tempo and in (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 this regard, the Mulabagal Rural Police have registered a case against driver of the said goods tempo.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending tempo, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- together with costs and interest.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending goods tempo, name, age,
avocation and income of petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the father of the petitioner.

Further admits that the vehicle bearing No.TN-91-AZ-6539 was covered under the policy of insurance issued by this respondent subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the alleged accident was occurred only due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the petitioner, (SCCH-3)
5 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 who was riding his Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner and without Suresh C.N vs Shivakumar on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146519518/
2 driving licence.

The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and at the time of accident the driver of the offending goods tempo had no valid and effective driving licence and and there is violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 and the compensation claimed is more excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.

05. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 28.11.2021 at about 08.30 a.m, near Nalluru Gate,
Mulbagal-Kolar, NH75 Road, Kolar, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Canter bearing registration No. TN-91-AZ-6539 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined Doctors as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondents did not lead evidence inspite of sufficient opportunity has been given.
Hence, the respondents evidence is taken as nil and closed their side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.

09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1
In affirmative  Issue No.2 In partly affirmative  Issue No.3

3 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioner filed affidavit as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments.
During the course of cross-examination he stated that after the accident he lost consciousness.

That he regain consciousness after 6-7 months of accident and that there was 2 feet distance from his vehicle to the goods tempo and it is not lorry and he admits that, in Ex.P.5 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 it is mentioned as "when I have proceeding in two- wheeler ahead to me a lorry was proceeding and hit against the lorry", but it is wrong.

I have not seen the offending tempo and denied to the suggestion that on the date of accident, he without wearing helmet and due to his negligent driving he hit against some other tempo and sustained injuries and admits that he has not seen the offending vehicle and he had not undergone any surgery at SNR hospital and there is no document to show that he was doing Dhobi business and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Mulbagal Rural Police in crime No.203/2021 for the offence punishable U/s 279, 337 of IPC against the driver of Canter.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving of Eicher vehicle bearing No.TN-91-AZ-6539 the accident took place and petitioner sustained injuries.
11. The accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Canter.

Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar showing place of accident near Nalluru Gate, Mulbagal-Kolar, NH75 Road, Kolar,
which is not disputed.
Ex.P.4 is IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident.
(SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 Ex.P.5 is MLC register which shows the place of accident is not disputed.
Ex.P.6 is the important document investigation officer.
After completion of the investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the Canter for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of IPC and Sec.177 of IMV Act.

Ex.P.7 is the Discharge summary which shows that the petitioner sustained communited sub trochanteric fracture of left femur with communited fracture of left patella, head injury and DM type 2 and the injuries are grievous in nature.
Ex.P.8 is another Discharge summary which shows that the petitioner sustained facial bone fracture and said injury is grievous in nature.
Ex.P.9 is another Discharge summary which shows that the petitioner sustained united fracture left patella with implant in situ and diabetes M ellitus and the injuries are grievous in nature.
Ex.P.12 is the Driving licence of the petitioner and Ex.P.13 is Aadhaar card of the petitioner.
These documents clearly goes to show that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Auto rickshaw.
To disprove the petitioner case, the respondents did not lead any (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 evidence.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

Petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy ans was aged about 38 years and was an agriculturist and dhobi and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc.,.
Due to accidental injuries he is bedridden and lost his income.

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any documents or evidence before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of authenticated, believable and satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the injured, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2021 to be taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.15,000/-.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his examination in chief that petitioner sustained comminuted subtrochanteric fracture of Lt. Femur with comminuted fracture of lt. patella and he assessed total disability of Lt. Lower limb at 50% and whole body disability of 25% and he has produced Outpatient card with examination report and X-ray as per Ex.P.16 and 17.
In his cross- examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally and fractures are united.

15. According to the evidence of PW.3, the Eye Specialist Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his examination in chief that petitioner sustained optic atrophy (left side) and he opined that vision in left eye is completely and irreversibly lost due to optic atrophy and he assessed visual disability is estimated to 30% as per guidelines of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and petitioner belongs to disability category II (one eyed person) and he has produced OPD card as per Ex.P.18.

He has seen Discharge summary and not (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 seen written statement and petitioner is type 2 diabetic patient and there is no mention of optic atrophy in Discharge summary.
16. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- As per Ex.P.7 to 9 Discharge summaries, the petitioner was admitted as inpatient nearly for 44 days in different hospitals.
During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment,
towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
17. Pain and sufferings:
As per Ex.P.5 MLC register and as per evidence of PW.2 and 3 Doctors and as per X-ray and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
18. Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding his income.
This (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.15,000/- per month and he was admitted in the hospital nearly for 44 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast three months.

Thus, taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Suresh C.N vs Shivakumar on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146519518/
5 Rs.45,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 3) under this head.
19.
Medical Expenses:-
The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.14, which amounts to Rs.8,14,520/- and prescriptions as per Ex.P.15.
On perusal of Sl. No.42, which is same bill of Sl. No.41 for Rs.5,000/-, hence same has to be deducted.

To disprove the said medical bills,
the respondent No.2 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Therefore, after deducting said amount, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,09,520/- under this head.

20. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

21. Looking to the nature of the injuries, it is duty of petitioner to prove his age, but petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show this exact date of birth.
However, he has produced notarized copies of Driving licence and Aadhaar card at Ex.P.12 and 13.

Eventhough said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age for any person,
but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 20.06.1980 and the alleged accident was occurred on 28.11.2021.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner as 41 years and this tribunal has assessed age of the petitioner is 41 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 years is '14'.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,74,520/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
25. Regarding liability:-
Though the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal, but not filed written statement and not contested the matter.

On service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement and contest the matter, but despsite sufficient opportunity, it has not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its contention.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 7 admits issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and same is valid as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 being the insurer of the offending Canter are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall deposit above said compensation amount of Rs.15,74,520/- from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:-

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,74,520/- (Rupees Fifteen lakhs seventy four thousand five hundred and twenty only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,74,520/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 being the insurer of the offending Canter are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,74,520/- (Rupees Fifteen lakhs seventy four thousand five hundred and twenty only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.3414/2022 petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
